subject: Media Literacy
title: Embracing Uncertainty
description: A fast breakdown of Embracing Uncertainty for builders.

hook.text: A breaking news story changes three times in one hour. Each version was presented as 'the truth.'

buildup.text: Intellectual humility — admitting uncertainty — is a powerful defense against misinformation.

discovery.text: People who say 'I'm not sure yet' are far less likely to spread false information than those who need instant answers.

twist.text: Social media punishes uncertainty. Confident, definitive posts get more engagement than nuanced, cautious ones.

climax.text: In a media landscape that rewards certainty, the bravest act is saying 'I need to verify this first.'

punchline.text: Saying 'I don't know yet' is smarter than being confidently wrong.

quiz.question: Why is intellectual humility a defense against misinformation?
options: Admitting uncertainty prevents you from sharing unverified claims
Humble people don't use social media
